_doc: Designated parity-bearing clauses between dogfood docs and their distributed template twins. Each clause stores ONLY markers (anchor + optional pattern), never the clause text — the compared value is read live from the canonical file, so this manifest cannot silently become a stale parallel copy of the clauses it guards (ADR-0050 §1 markers-only discipline). Keep it small and curated: add an entry only for a clause that MUST stay identical across the twin pair. `pattern` (a Python regex) extracts the discriminating value(s) from the canonical section; every captured value must also appear in the twin section. Omit `pattern` to compare the whole normalized section body. Curated §-content clauses (per ADR-0056: the template twin is a derived artifact whose §-content mirror must not silently drift — the class that recurred across PB-0048/0049/0051). Add a clause here whenever a bionic/CLAUDE.md §-edit MUST reach the CLAUDE.md.tmpl twin; a naive full-section diff is deliberately avoided because the twin diverges by design (ADR tokens stripped, downstream-shaped).

§4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface report shape — six H2 sections in order, the summary table's place, the one data-framing note, and the grandfather date
clauses.pattern: exactly six H2 sections in the order Propose, Amend, Repair, Revoke, Keep, Coverage|one summary table between its title and|and exactly one data-framing note|a report dated on or before that date keeps the sections and the notes it was written with|The five-finding per-pass cap counts across Propose, Amend, Repair and Revoke combined|Keep, Coverage, the summary table and the Revoke dispositions count against no cap|Keep, Coverage and the Revoke dispositions define no finding|the summary table defines none, carrying in each row an id one of the four finding sections already defines|Keep and the Revoke dispositions carry no finding id at all|Coverage carries a finding id only where a lifecycle record references one|so the no-definition clause governs Coverage unchanged|that row id set equals the set of ids the four finding sections define|equal counts alone do not satisfy it|A disagreement between the two sets is refused rather than counted around

clauses.section: §6 the `adr-review` op body: the four finding sections in order, and that Keep and Coverage carry no count
clauses.pattern: the finding definition counts across the four finding sections|\(Propose, Amend, Repair, Revoke\); Keep and Coverage define no finding, so neither carries a count

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface write set — five paths, six writes, the two op kinds, and both rule handles
clauses.pattern: Its write set is closed and holds exactly five paths|the dated report under the reviews directory, the derived reviews index, the operational log, the current month's journal file, and the journal index|writes six times across those five, because the log takes two ops|one `adr-review` op written by the review itself|one `journal` op written by `log-work`|beside the journal entry and the journal index row|rule:review-write-set-five-paths|rule:review-proposes-and-enacts-nothing

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface lifecycle-record table under `## Coverage`, the `report_grammar` frontmatter discriminator, and the filename-date binding the regenerator checks against frontmatter `date`
clauses.pattern: Lifecycle records live in a five-column table under `## Coverage`|source report date, finding id, pass, event, locator|identified by its own header row rather than by its position|so it never merges with the per-goal coverage matrix|A report declares its grammar through the frontmatter key `report_grammar`|whose one recognised value is `lifecycle`|A report carrying no key reads under the frozen legacy counting rule|a report dated after 2026-09-08 carrying no key is refused|an unrecognised value is refused; neither is defaulted|That date is the report's filename date, which the regenerator checks against the frontmatter

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the reviews index splits raised from standing, and a legacy row carries the literal `unknown`
clauses.pattern: The generated reviews index distinguishes findings raised from current standing|a legacy row carries the literal `unknown` as a positive value|never blank, never omitted, never `0`, and never recomputed from later records|A legacy row that raised nothing renders the bare literal `unknown` with no count|its `raised` cell reads `0 \(legacy\)`

clauses.section: §4 journal write rules: a composed body never leaves a fence open
clauses.pattern: (?m)^- \*\*A composed body never leaves a fence open\*\*[^\n]*$
